title: Pancreas
summary: The pancreas is a small gland behind the stomach with two big jobs: it makes digestive juices that help break down food, and it makes hormones like insulin that control sugar in your blood. Explore its dual role in digestion and blood-sugar balance.

compareCandidate.label: Pancreas vs. liver
compareCandidate.description: Both help digestion, but differently. The liver makes bile (stored in the gallbladder) to help digest fats and cleans the blood. The pancreas makes digestive enzymes and the hormone insulin.

processes: Making insulin to control blood sugar
Sending enzymes to the small intestine
plainLanguageExplanation: The pancreas is a soft, elongated gland tucked behind the stomach. It has two very different jobs. For digestion, it makes pancreatic juice - a liquid full of enzymes - and sends it to the small intestine to help break down proteins, fats, and carbs. For balance, it makes hormones (especially insulin) and releases them into the blood. Insulin signals cells to take in sugar from the blood, keeping blood-sugar levels steady. So the pancreas is both a digestion helper and a blood-sugar controller.

whyItMatters: The pancreas is the body's two-in-one gland: it helps digest food AND keeps blood sugar balanced. Understanding it explains how your body handles the sugar in snacks and why diabetes is related to this small organ.
didYouKnow: Your pancreas releases about 1.5 liters of digestive juice a day - and insulin, one of its hormones, is the key to how your body uses sugar.
